stories.title: Handle WhatsApp BSUID (Business-Scoped User ID) in message routing
stories.description: Starting June 2026, WhatsApp will introduce usernames that allow users to hide their phone numbers, replacing the `from` field in webhooks with a BSUID (up to 128 alphanumeric chars, format `CC.BSUID`). The system must persist and route on BSUID alongside phone numbers to avoid losing conversation continuity when a user adopts a username.
acceptanceCriteria: Incoming Baileys/Cloud API messages extract `bsuid` from the sender identifier when it is not an E.164 number
BSUID is stored in `rainbow_conversations` and contact records alongside the phone number column
Conversation lookup falls back to BSUID when phone number is absent
Existing phone-number-keyed records are merged with their BSUID when both are present in the same message
Unit tests cover routing for E.164-only, BSUID-only, and dual-identifier payloads
technicalNotes: Baileys surfaces this as the `lid` (linked identity) field on incoming messages
Format is `CC.BSUID` where CC is a two-letter country code; store raw value, strip prefix for lookup
See: https://www.twilio.com/en-us/changelog/whatsapp-usernames--new-business-scoped-user-id--bsuid--field-re

stories.title: Subscribe to and handle WhatsApp account_update webhook (violations and restrictions)
stories.description: The `account_update` webhook field fires when Meta imposes a policy violation (`ACCOUNT_VIOLATION` with a `violation_type`) or account restriction (`ACCOUNT_RESTRICTION` with expiry). Without subscribing, a ban or throttle is invisible until message delivery silently fails, making root-cause analysis very slow.
acceptanceCriteria: The system subscribes to the `account_update` webhook field on startup (or validates subscription exists)
On receiving `ACCOUNT_VIOLATION`, an admin alert is sent via the existing notification channel with the violation_type included
On receiving `ACCOUNT_RESTRICTION`, the restriction expiry timestamp is logged and surfaced in /health or admin dashboard
A structured log entry is emitted for each account_update event with field `event`, `phone_number`, `violation_type` or `restriction_info`
Integration test verifies the webhook handler correctly parses both violation and restriction payloads
technicalNotes: Payload shape: `changes[0].field = 'account_update'`, `value.event = 'ACCOUNT_VIOLATION'`, `value.violation_info.violation_type`
Restriction payload uses `value.restriction_info` array with each entry having `restriction_type` and `expiration`
See: https://hookdeck.com/webhooks/platforms/guide-to-whatsapp-webhooks-features-and-best-practices

stories.title: Subscribe to business_capability_update webhook and react to tier changes
stories.description: The `business_capability_update` webhook fires when WhatsApp changes the WABA's messaging tier (max daily conversations per phone). Since October 2025, limits are enforced at the business portfolio level. Reacting in real time allows the system to update its per-profile send-rate governor without a manual configuration change.
acceptanceCriteria: System subscribes to the `business_capability_update` webhook field
On receipt, the new `max_daily_conversation_per_phone` value is stored in config/DB
The per-profile rate limit manager reads the stored tier cap value on startup and on each webhook update
An admin log entry records each tier change with old and new values
A test verifies the handler parses the payload and updates the config correctly
technicalNotes: Payload field: `changes[0].field = 'business_capability_update'`, `value.max_daily_conversation_per_phone`
As of Q2 2026, Meta is removing the 2K and 10K tiers — any business completing verification moves straight to 100K
See: https://developers.facebook.com/docs/whatsapp/messaging-limits/

stories.title: Add Meta CA certificate trust store update for mTLS webhook continuity
stories.description: Meta is replacing DigiCert with its own CA for mTLS-secured webhook delivery, effective 31 March 2026. Any server with mTLS verification will start failing TLS handshakes on 1 April 2026, causing total webhook blackout. The new certificate (`meta-outbound-api-ca-2025-12.pem`) must be added to the trust store before that date.
acceptanceCriteria: The deployment playbook (`deploy.sh` or `ecosystem.config.cjs`) documents the CA trust store update step
A startup health check verifies that the Meta CA cert is present in the Node.js `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` or system trust store
A warning log is emitted at startup if the cert is missing and the current date is within 60 days of 2026-04-01
The certificate file is checked into `deploy/certs/meta-outbound-api-ca-2025-12.pem` (not in secrets)
technicalNotes: Set `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/path/to/meta-outbound-api-ca-2025-12.pem` in PM2 ecosystem config
Alternatively, append cert to system CA store in Lightsail Ubuntu via `update-ca-certificates`
See: https://chatarmin.com/en/blog/whatsapp-webhooks

stories.title: Replace useMultiFileAuthState with custom DB-backed Baileys auth state
stories.description: The Baileys library explicitly documents that `useMultiFileAuthState` must NOT be used in production due to excessive I/O. On the Lightsail 450 MB memory-capped process, file-system churn for every credential update causes latency spikes and risks auth state corruption on OOM. A PostgreSQL-backed auth state persists credentials atomically.
acceptanceCriteria: A `useDbAuthState(profileId)` function is implemented that reads/writes Baileys `AuthenticationCreds` and signal keys to a dedicated `baileys_auth_state` table
Credential updates use upsert (not insert+delete) to prevent write amplification
Signal key writes are batched: keys are buffered for 100 ms and written in a single transaction
On reconnection after crash, the system restores from DB without requiring QR re-scan
The existing `useMultiFileAuthState` call in `src/lib/baileys-client.ts` is removed
A test verifies that a credential save followed by process restart and reload returns the same creds
technicalNotes: Baileys auth state interface requires `state.creds` (JSON) and `state.keys` object with `get`/`set` methods
Signal protocol keys must be namespaced by type (pre-key, session, sender-key, etc.)
See Baileys docs: https://baileys.wiki/docs/socket/connecting/

stories.title: Configure Express HTTP server keep-alive and headers timeouts to prevent 502s
stories.description: Node.js HTTP server defaults (`keepAliveTimeout` = 5 s, `headersTimeout` = 60 s) are shorter than typical load balancer idle timeouts (AWS default: 60 s), causing intermittent 502 errors when the server closes a keep-alive connection just as the load balancer reuses it. Explicitly configuring these values prevents the race condition.
acceptanceCriteria: Express server sets `keepAliveTimeout = 65000` ms (> AWS ALB default 60 s)
Express server sets `headersTimeout = 66000` ms (> keepAliveTimeout per Node.js recommendation)
Express server sets `requestTimeout = 30000` ms to bound hung request sockets
Values are configurable via environment variables `SERVER_KEEP_ALIVE_TIMEOUT`, `SERVER_HEADERS_TIMEOUT`, `SERVER_REQUEST_TIMEOUT`
A startup log entry records the configured timeout values
The settings are documented in `.env.example`
technicalNotes: Set via `server.keepAliveTimeout`, `server.headersTimeout`, `server.requestTimeout` on the http.Server instance returned by `app.listen()`
Also set `server.setTimeout(socketTimeout)` to destroy hung sockets not covered by request/headers timeout
See: https://betterstack.com/community/guides/scaling-nodejs/nodejs-timeouts/

stories.title: Implement keep-alive connection draining on graceful shutdown
stories.description: The existing graceful shutdown (`SIGTERM` handler) calls `server.close()` but does not drain idle keep-alive connections, leaving the process hanging until PM2's kill timeout. Node.js 18.2 introduced `server.closeIdleConnections()`, which should be called immediately on SIGTERM to unblock the close, while active requests continue to drain.
acceptanceCriteria: On `SIGTERM`, `server.closeIdleConnections()` is called immediately after `server.close()`
Active requests are allowed up to 15 s to complete before `server.closeAllConnections()` is called
BullMQ workers are paused (stop accepting new jobs) before the HTTP server is closed
Database pool is destroyed only after HTTP server and BullMQ workers have stopped
PM2 `kill_timeout` in `ecosystem.config.cjs` is set to 20000 ms to align with the drain budget
A test simulates SIGTERM with an in-flight request and verifies the response completes before process exit
technicalNotes: `server.closeIdleConnections()` is available from Node.js 18.2 — confirm runtime version satisfies this
`server.closeAllConnections()` (Node.js 18.2) destroys all connections regardless of active requests — use only as final fallback
See: https://betterstack.com/community/guides/scaling-nodejs/nodejs-graceful-shutdown/

stories.title: Emit OTel gen_ai agent spans with conversation_id for multi-turn tracing
stories.description: The OTel GenAI semantic conventions v1.40.0 define `invoke_agent` span types with `gen_ai.agent.id`, `gen_ai.agent.name`, `gen_ai.conversation.id`, and `gen_ai.tool.definitions` attributes. The current instrumentation emits only per-LLM-call spans; wrapping the full pipeline execution in an `invoke_agent` span enables end-to-end tracing of multi-turn conversations.
acceptanceCriteria: Each message pipeline execution is wrapped in a parent `invoke_agent` span named `invoke_agent Rainbow`
The span includes `gen_ai.agent.name = 'Rainbow'`, `gen_ai.conversation.id` (the conversation UUID), `gen_ai.provider.name`
Child LLM call spans are nested under the agent span
Tool execution (MCP tool calls) emits child `execute_tool` spans with `gen_ai.tool.name` and `gen_ai.tool.call.id`
`gen_ai.response.finish_reasons` and token usage attributes are set on the agent span from the aggregated LLM call
Span kind is `INTERNAL` (in-process agent, not a remote agent service)
technicalNotes: OTel spec: `gen_ai.operation.name = 'invoke_agent'`, span name = `invoke_agent {gen_ai.agent.name}`
Use `tracer.startActiveSpan()` at pipeline entry so all child spans are automatically nested
`gen_ai.conversation.id` should be the stable conversation UUID already stored in `rainbow_conversations`
See: https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/gen-ai-agent-spans/

stories.title: Capture opt-in gen_ai.client.inference.operation.details events for LLM audit
stories.description: OTel GenAI semantic conventions define the opt-in `gen_ai.client.inference.operation.details` event that captures full prompt/response payloads, system instructions, and tool definitions on the same span. This is the standardized replacement for ad-hoc LLM request logging, enabling structured audit trails in observability back-ends (Grafana, Jaeger).
acceptanceCriteria: When `OTEL_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT=true` env var is set, the `gen_ai.client.inference.operation.details` event is emitted on each LLM span
The event body includes `gen_ai.input.messages`, `gen_ai.output.messages`, `gen_ai.system_instructions`, and `gen_ai.tool.definitions`
When the env var is absent or false, no message content is captured (default-off for privacy)
PII redaction middleware (if implemented) runs before the event is emitted
Unit test verifies event is emitted when opt-in and absent when not
technicalNotes: Use `span.addEvent('gen_ai.client.inference.operation.details', attributes)` via the OTel Logs API event bridge
Add a separate app-level flag `OTEL_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT` to independently control message capture
See: https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/gen-ai-events/

stories.title: Implement BullMQ FlowProducer for multi-stage message pipeline with child job dependencies
stories.description: Complex message handling (e.g., transcribe audio → classify intent → generate LLM reply → send response) currently chains steps imperatively, making error attribution and partial retry impossible. BullMQ FlowProducer's parent-child dependency model allows each stage to be a discrete job that retries independently; the parent only executes after all children complete.
acceptanceCriteria: A `FlowProducer` instance is created and registered alongside the existing BullMQ queue
A multi-step flow is defined: `[preprocess-media, classify-intent, generate-reply]` as children of a `send-response` parent
Each child job has `failParentOnFailure: true` so a failed classification aborts the send
Child results are aggregated via `getChildrenValues()` inside the parent worker
Dead letter queue (already implemented) receives parent jobs whose children permanently fail
The flow job IDs do not contain colons (per BullMQ restriction)
A test verifies that completing all children moves the parent from `waiting-children` to `waiting`
technicalNotes: FlowProducer.add() accepts `{ name, data, queueName, children: [...] }` — parent queue can differ from child queues
Job IDs must not contain `:` as BullMQ uses them as separators for dependency tracking
See: https://docs.bullmq.io/guide/flows

stories.title: Add BullMQ priority aging to prevent starvation of low-priority message jobs
stories.description: High-volume marketing campaigns can queue thousands of low-priority jobs. Without priority aging, genuinely time-sensitive low-priority messages (e.g., guest checkout reminders added after a campaign) starve indefinitely. A periodic worker upgrades job priority based on wait time, ensuring all jobs eventually get processed.
acceptanceCriteria: A cron-based BullMQ worker runs every 2 minutes and calls `job.changePriority()` on jobs waiting longer than a configurable threshold (default: 10 minutes)
Priority is incremented by 1 for every 5 minutes of wait time (up to a minimum priority of 1)
The aging worker emits a metric counter `bullmq.priority_aged_jobs` for each job it promotes
The aging threshold and increment are configurable via admin settings
A test verifies that a priority-3 job waiting 15 minutes is promoted to priority-1 after aging runs
technicalNotes: BullMQ priorities: 1 = highest, 2,097,152 = lowest; default (no priority) is processed before all prioritized jobs
Use `Queue.getJobs(['prioritized'])` to retrieve jobs eligible for aging
`job.changePriority({ priority: newValue })` is the runtime mutation API
See: https://docs.bullmq.io/guide/jobs/prioritized

stories.title: Add WhatsApp phone_number_name_update webhook handler for display name change alerts
stories.description: The `phone_number_name_update` webhook field fires when Meta approves or rejects a WABA display name change request. Without a handler, name change approvals are invisible to operators; a rejected name silently continues displaying the old name without any alert. Handling this event enables the admin dashboard to surface display name status.
acceptanceCriteria: System subscribes to the `phone_number_name_update` webhook field
On approval, the new display name is stored in the profile config and reflected in the admin dashboard
On rejection, an admin alert is sent with the rejection reason
A structured log entry is emitted with `event = 'phone_number_name_update'`, `decision` (APPROVED/REJECTED), and `rejected_reason` when present
Unit test covers both approval and rejection payload parsing
technicalNotes: Payload: `changes[0].field = 'phone_number_name_update'`, `value.display_phone_number`, `value.decision` (APPROVED/REJECTED), `value.rejected_reason`
See: https://hookdeck.com/webhooks/platforms/guide-to-whatsapp-webhooks-features-and-best-practices

stories.title: Add WhatsApp security webhook handler for suspicious login alerts
stories.description: The `security` webhook field fires on security-related WABA events such as suspicious login attempts. This is distinct from account_update and provides early warning of account compromise before an outright ban occurs. The event must trigger an immediate high-severity admin notification.
acceptanceCriteria: System subscribes to the `security` webhook field
On receipt, a high-severity admin notification is dispatched immediately (not batched)
The raw webhook payload is persisted to an audit log table with timestamp and profile_id
A startup check verifies the `security` field subscription is active
Unit test covers payload parsing and notification dispatch
technicalNotes: This is a separate subscribable field from `account_update`; both should be subscribed
Log the raw payload verbatim in addition to structured fields since exact payload structure varies
See: https://hookdeck.com/webhooks/platforms/guide-to-whatsapp-webhooks-features-and-best-practices

stories.title: Implement LLM streaming response with SSE for admin webchat panel
stories.description: The admin webchat panel currently waits for the full LLM response before rendering, causing 3-8 s of blank response time. Streaming via Server-Sent Events (SSE) displays tokens incrementally as they arrive, matching user expectations set by modern AI interfaces. The pipeline already has a conversation SSE route; LLM token streaming should be plumbed through it.
acceptanceCriteria: The LLM client supports a streaming mode that yields token chunks via an async generator
The admin webchat SSE endpoint emits `data: {token}` events for each chunk
A `[DONE]` sentinel event is emitted after the final token
The non-streaming path (WhatsApp reply) remains unchanged; streaming is only used for the webchat UI
Backpressure is handled: if the SSE client disconnects mid-stream, the LLM request is aborted via AbortController
Works with all three providers (NVIDIA, Ollama, OpenRouter) — falls back to non-streaming if provider does not support it
technicalNotes: OpenAI-compatible endpoints use `stream: true` and return `data: {choices: [{delta: {content: '...'}}]}`
Use `res.setHeader('Content-Type', 'text/event-stream')` and `res.flushHeaders()` before the first token
AbortController should be tied to `res.on('close', ...)` to cancel the LLM request on client disconnect

stories.title: Add CSRF double-submit cookie protection to admin session endpoints
stories.description: Admin endpoints that mutate state (config writes, KB uploads, conversation exports) use cookie-based session authentication, making them vulnerable to CSRF if a forged cross-origin request is submitted. The deprecated `csurf` middleware has unfixed CVEs; the current best practice combines SameSite=Strict cookies with a custom CSRF token in a non-cookie header.
acceptanceCriteria: All state-changing admin routes (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) require a `X-CSRF-Token` header matching a per-session CSRF token
The CSRF token is issued on admin login and accessible via `GET /api/csrf-token` (JSON, not cookie)
Session cookie is set with `SameSite=Strict; Secure; HttpOnly`
GET/HEAD/OPTIONS requests are exempt from the CSRF check
403 is returned when CSRF token is missing or invalid
A Playwright test verifies that a cross-origin POST without the CSRF token is rejected
technicalNotes: Do NOT use the deprecated `csurf` npm package (last release 2021, unfixed CVEs)
Implement custom middleware: generate token with `crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('hex')`, store in session, compare on each mutating request
See: https://corgea.com/Learn/express-js-security-best-practices-2025

stories.title: Implement WhatsApp portfolio pacing awareness and adaptive send-rate throttle
stories.description: Since late 2025, Meta enforces pacing at the business portfolio level: large campaign sends are batched and paused if feedback signals turn negative. Without pacing awareness, the system may queue thousands of outbound messages that Meta holds back, causing phantom delivery failures. An adaptive send-rate governor reduces blast throughput when portfolio quality signals degrade.
acceptanceCriteria: The outbound message scheduler monitors the `phone_number_quality_update` webhook for FLAGGED events
When the quality rating drops to YELLOW, the outbound send rate is halved automatically
When the quality rating drops to RED or FLAGGED, all non-session outbound messages (templates) are paused
Quality state is stored per phone-number profile and reflected in the admin dashboard
Paused template messages remain in the BullMQ queue (not dropped) and are resumed when quality recovers to GREEN
A test verifies the throttle logic activates and deactivates correctly on simulated quality events
technicalNotes: Portfolio pacing is a Meta-side mechanism; the app reduces throughput proactively to avoid compounding the issue
Quality webhook payload: `changes[0].field = 'phone_number_quality_update'`, `value.current_limit`, `value.event` (FLAGGED/UNFLAGGED)
See: https://woztell.com/whatsapp-api-2026-updates-pacing-limits-usernames/

stories.title: Add OTel gen_ai.usage.cache_read.input_tokens tracking for prompt cache hits
stories.description: OTel GenAI semantic conventions v1.40.0 define `gen_ai.usage.cache_read.input_tokens` and `gen_ai.usage.cache_creation.input_tokens` attributes. Providers like Anthropic and NVIDIA return cache hit/miss counts in their response metadata. Tracking these values reveals the effectiveness of system-prompt caching and directly correlates to cost savings.
acceptanceCriteria: When the LLM response includes cache token metadata, `gen_ai.usage.cache_read.input_tokens` and `gen_ai.usage.cache_creation.input_tokens` are set on the OTel span
A Prometheus counter `genai_cache_read_tokens_total` and `genai_cache_creation_tokens_total` are incremented per provider
The LLM cost tracker accounts for cached vs uncached token rates
Unit test verifies attribute extraction from Anthropic-format response metadata (`usage.cache_read_input_tokens`)
technicalNotes: Anthropic response: `usage.cache_read_input_tokens`, `usage.cache_creation_input_tokens`
OTel attribute names: `gen_ai.usage.cache_read.input_tokens`, `gen_ai.usage.cache_creation.input_tokens`
See: https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/gen-ai-spans/

stories.title: Add AbortSignal.timeout for all outbound HTTP calls to external services
stories.description: Node.js `fetch` calls to DIGIMAN API, LLM providers, and WhatsApp Cloud API have no timeout by default, meaning a slow upstream can hold a BullMQ worker slot indefinitely and exhaust the pool. `AbortSignal.timeout(ms)` (available since Node.js 17.3) provides a per-request deadline without requiring a separate `setTimeout` cleanup.
acceptanceCriteria: All `fetch()` calls to external services pass `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(ms)` with provider-appropriate timeouts: LLM = 30 s, DIGIMAN = 10 s, WhatsApp Cloud API = 15 s
On `AbortError`, the error is logged with `error.type = 'timeout'` and the upstream name
Timeout durations are configurable via environment variables: `LLM_TIMEOUT_MS`, `DIGIMAN_TIMEOUT_MS`, `WA_API_TIMEOUT_MS`
Existing retry logic (exponential backoff) treats `AbortError` as a retryable error (not a permanent failure)
A unit test verifies that a mocked upstream that delays beyond the timeout triggers an AbortError and retry
technicalNotes: `AbortSignal.timeout(30000)` — no cleanup needed, the signal is garbage collected automatically
Do NOT reuse the same AbortSignal across retries — create a fresh one per attempt
See: https://betterstack.com/community/guides/scaling-nodejs/nodejs-timeouts/

stories.title: Subscribe to WhatsApp flows webhook field and add health-check ping handler
stories.description: The `flows` webhook subscription field is required to receive endpoint availability notifications for WhatsApp Flows integrations. Without this subscription, failed Flow endpoint calls are silent. Additionally, the WhatsApp Flows spec requires the endpoint responds to a `ping` action within 5 s or Meta marks the endpoint as unavailable.
acceptanceCriteria: System subscribes to the `flows` webhook field on startup
The existing WhatsApp Flows endpoint handles `{ action: 'ping' }` by returning `{ data: { status: 'active' } }` within 2 s
Flow endpoint response time is tracked as a custom metric `flows_endpoint_response_ms`
A liveness probe in `/health/live` includes Flows endpoint self-test status
Unit test verifies the ping response format matches Meta's specification
technicalNotes: Flows health-check action: `{ version: '3.0', action: 'ping' }` — respond with `{ version: '3.0', data: { status: 'active' } }`
AES-GCM decryption is required for non-ping requests (already implemented)
See: https://developers.facebook.com/docs/whatsapp/flows/reference/flowswebhooks/
